question: Settling down of heavier insoluble components of a mixture of water and insoluble substances is called:
solution:
The correct answer is **__Sedimentation.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The process of separating insoluble substances which are heavier than liquid by allowing them to settle down on their own due to gravity is called** **sedimentation**.
 
• **Sedimentation is the process of deposition of sediments.**
 
• It tooks place when particles in suspension are settled out of the fluid in which they are entrained and come to rest against a barrier.
 
• The particles which settled out from the suspension become sediment, and in water treatment is called as **sludge.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evaporation** is a procedure of vaporization which occurs on the surface of a liquid as it changes into the gas phase. 
 
• **Decantation **is the process of separation of liquid from solid and other non-merging liquids.
 
• **The process in which solid particles in a liquid or gaseous fluid are removed by the use of a filter medium that permits the fluid to pass through but retains the solid particles**.
